_note: The hub restates a number from every page it links to. Each restatement is re-run HERE against THAT PAGE'S OWN shipped data file, so a correction on a page fails this page's gate instead of leaving a stale card behind. That is the defect this file exists to catch: the editorial contract says hub cards stay in sync with corrected pages, and nothing enforced it. Paths climb out of index/data/ on purpose.

claims.official_check: Re-run derive_index.py and diff counts.json; a non-empty diff means the shipped file was stale.

claims.assert: (lambda P: sorted(P) == sorted(k[3:] for k in D if k.startswith('cj_')) and all(P[s]['claims'] == len(D['cj_' + s]['claims']) and P[s]['manual'] == sum(1 for c in D['cj_' + s]['claims'] if c.get('verify') == 'manual') for s in P))(D['counts']['pages'])
claims.actual: sorted((s, r['claims'], len(D['cj_' + s]['claims'])) for s, r in D['counts']['pages'].items() if r['claims'] != len(D['cj_' + s]['claims']))
claims.falsified_if: A page gains or loses a claim and derive_index.py is not re-run, or an artifact is added to the tree without a cj_ entry here. THIS IS THE GUARD THAT WAS MISSING. index-counts-internal only ever checked counts.json against itself, so a stale file stayed internally consistent and kept passing: on 2026-08-29 every page had grown and the shipped file still said 292 claims across thirteen pages, which is how the cluster-health card advertised 23 claims for a page that says on its own face there are 27 of them. A hub card's claim count is a statement about another page, and the only honest way to hold one is to read that page. The fix is never to retype a count; it is to re-run derive_index.py.
claims.official_check: python _data/build/derive_index.py, then git diff index/data/counts.json — an empty diff is the pass.

claims.text: The hub links fifteen pages carrying 401 checked claims, 15 of which rest on a document a person read; and two further artifacts in the tree are deliberately not linked. Re-blessed 2026-08-30 when the patents page shipped with 7 claims: the first new analysis page since sources, filling the innovation gap four reviewers named, and the register grew to fifteen datasets with it.
claims.source: index/data/counts.json against the fourteen card anchors in index/index.html and the withheld-pages paragraph beside them; the exclusions are declared in scorecard/.unlisted and accountability/.unlisted
claims.assert: (lambda P, U, L: sorted(set(P) - U) == L and len(L) == 15 and U <= set(P) and len(P) - len(L) == 2 and D['counts']['n_pieces'] == len(P) and sum(P[s]['claims'] for s in L) == 401 and sum(P[s]['manual'] for s in L) == 15)(D['counts']['pages'], {'scorecard', 'accountability'}, ['churn', 'cluster-health', 'cost-scissors', 'federal-money', 'funding-map', 'laborshed', 'location-quotient', 'occupations', 'patents', 'peers', 'realwage', 'revisions', 'sources', 'timeline', 'wages'])
claims.actual: (sorted(set(D['counts']['pages']) - {'scorecard', 'accountability'}), len(D['counts']['pages']), sum(p['claims'] for s, p in D['counts']['pages'].items() if s not in ('scorecard', 'accountability')), sum(p['manual'] for s, p in D['counts']['pages'].items() if s not in ('scorecard', 'accountability')))
claims.falsified_if: A page is added to or removed from the tree, or any linked page gains or loses a claim. This is the only guard on the three inventory literals the page prints without scripting — fourteen pages, 373 claims, 15 manual — and on the count of withheld pages in the paragraph under them, and it is deliberately intolerant: those literals are a rendered snapshot of a computation app.js re-runs at load, so any drift has to be re-blessed by a person rather than absorbed. It is also the enforcement of the .unlisted convention: a bundled page makes no external requests and cannot read a .unlisted file at render time, so a new artifact that is neither carded here nor named in this assertion fails the gate until someone decides which it is. The 'two withheld' clause is what keeps the second sentence honest in the other direction: carding one of the two without deleting its .unlisted file, or deleting the file without carding it, breaks this before it reaches a reader.

The award-to-average ratio is printed to one decimal, so 1.35 or 1.45 breaks it. THE BASIS IS THE POINT OF THIS ASSERTION. An annual rate may not include a year that has not finished: fiscal 2026 stands at $23.0 million part-way through and dragged the mean down to $34.9 million, understating the routine flow and overstating the award at 1.5 years of it, while the cluster-health dashboard printed the finished-years pair. The maximum is the guard on the card's other sentence: 'fiscal 2019 alone cleared the award line' is only readable beside a range whose top is above $51.0M.

THE TWO RUBBER FIGURES ARE NOT A DISAGREEMENT AND THIS CLAIM EXISTS TO KEEP THEM DISTINGUISHABLE. This card said 'Rubber products, the industry Akron is named for, run 2.44 times' while cluster-health said 'Plastics and rubber, the industries the region is known for, run 2.32 times'; two readers, and one cross-page audit, filed that as one figure printed at two values. claims.assert: (lambda T, S: T['awards'] == 85_335_784 and T['match'] == 20_954_667 and T['total'] == 106_290_451 and T['awards'] + T['match'] == T['total'] and T['awards'] == sum(s['award'] for s in S) and T['match'] == sum(s['matchAmount'] for s in S) and len(S) == 3 and max(s['award'] for s in S) == D['hub']['award'] and round(T['awards'] / 1e6, 1) + round(T['match'] / 1e6, 1) == round(T['total'] / 1e6, 1) == 106.3)(D['fm']['meta']['totals'], D['fm']['sources']) and len(D['fm']['recipients']) == 21

They do not have to in general — three figures rounded to a tenth can miss their own total by a tenth — which is exactly why this is asserted rather than assumed.

claims.text: Revisions card, answer line and finding: almost every number moves. 259 of 273 published months in three producer-price series were changed later, by a typical 0.15 percent.
claims.source: ALFRED archival vintages, three PPI series, 2019-2026, via revisions/data/revisions.json
claims.assert: len(D['rev']['periods']) == 259 and len(set((r['series'], r['date']) for r in D['rev']['all'])) == 273 and 0.145 <= (lambda a: (lambda s, n: s[n//2] if n % 2 else (s[n//2-1] + s[n//2]) / 2)(sorted(a), len(a)))([abs(p['pct']) for p in D['rev']['periods'] if p['pct'] is not None]) < 0.155 and 0.9 <= len(D['rev']['periods']) / len(set((r['series'], r['date']) for r in D['rev']['all'])) < 1

The last clause is what carries the word 'almost': the revised share has to stay at or above 90 percent and strictly below all of them. The card said 'Every number moves' while its own finding said 259 of 273, which is 94.9 percent; 'almost' is the word the data supports and the assertion now fails if either half of it stops being true. The scope is those three series and the card says so; it is not a statement about this site's figures generally.

claims.source: OMB metropolitan statistical area delineations (Bulletin 23-01), the same delineations BLS applies to the OEWS metropolitan wage files this site reads. Ashtabula County is the Ashtabula micropolitan area and Wayne County is the Wooster micropolitan area; neither is part of an MSA.
